title: Factorising linear expressions by grouping
summary: Group four-term linear expressions, expose a common binomial factor, and verify the product by expansion.
objectives: Choose useful pairs of terms and extract their common factors.
Recognise and factor a repeated binomial.
Handle reordered terms and negative common factors accurately.

blocks.text: Factorising rewrites a sum as a product. In a four-term expression, useful grouping creates the same bracket from two pairs. For ax+bx+kay+kby, group the x-terms and y-terms: x(a+b)+ky(a+b). The repeated bracket can then be factored out.
The final product is (a+b)(x+ky). Expanding it reproduces all four original terms. This reverse-expansion check is the most reliable way to confirm that no coefficient or sign was lost.

sections.title: Choose groups that reveal a common bracket

blocks.text: Terms are sometimes presented in an inconvenient order. Reorder them before grouping, keeping each sign attached. Look for coefficient ratios or shared variable patterns that suggest which terms belong together.

After taking the highest common factor from each group, the bracketed expressions must match exactly. If they differ only by sign, factor a negative number from one group so that both brackets have the same order and signs.

First remove any common factor shared by all four terms. Then apply grouping to what remains. A response is fully factorised when no factor contains a further common numerical or algebraic factor appropriate to the syllabus.

Expand the final pair of brackets term by term and compare with the original expression. Pay particular attention to a negative factor: multiplying it through must recreate the original signs, not merely the same variables.
